item.title: Zahed: Legal action to be taken over harassment of Dr Yunus in US
item.description:
Legal action will be taken over the alleged harassment of former interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus in the United States, Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman has said.
He said the government would follow the same legal process adopted after actress Azmeri Haque Badhon was harassed in Italy last month.
Zahed made the remarks at a regular press briefing at the Secretariat on Tuesday in response to questions from journalists about the incident involving Yunus.
A video circulating on social media shows Dr Yunus leaving John F Kennedy Airport in New York in a wheelchair, with several people approaching him and shouting slogans. The protesters were heard making abusive remarks, including asking why he had come to the United States.
Supporters of the banned Awami League living abroad have been accused of being involved in the incident.
Responding to questions, Zahed said: “I am aware of the legal process initiated after our actress Azmeri Haque Badhon was harassed. The same will happen in this case. I want to tell the Awami League ‘terrorists’ abroad that if they attempt such actions, it will not go unchallenged.”
The adviser also said the government would examine whether there had been any lapse in the protocol and status accorded to Dr Yunus, who served as chief adviser to the interim government.
Asked about the prospects for political reconciliation, Zahed said he saw no possibility of reconciliation with the Awami League, citing what he described as a lack of remorse among its leaders and their threats.

item.title: Old Dhaka fire safety recommendations remain unimplemented
item.description:
Old Dhaka continues to face serious fire risks, with thousands of chemical warehouses and factories operating in densely populated neighbourhoods despite repeated deadly blazes and years of recommendations from the fire service.
An estimated 25,000 small and large chemical warehouses are scattered across the area, leaving residents exposed to hazardous materials. Recommendations made by the fire service to reduce fire risks have remained largely unimplemented, allowing even small fires to escalate into major incidents.
On Monday, a fire broke out at Manjur Khan Plaza market in Chawkbazar. Five units initially responded, but the blaze intensified. It took 10 units around 12 hours to bring the fire under control. Narrow streets hampered the movement of firefighting vehicles, while plastic products and flammable materials at the site made the operation more difficult.
Officials and experts said implementing the fire service’s recommendations could help contain fires more quickly and reduce casualties.
Old Dhaka has witnessed devastating fires in Nimtoli in 2010 and Churihatta in 2019. The Nimtoli fire on June 3, 2010, killed 124 people, while the Churihatta fire claimed 71 lives.
Following both tragedies, senior government officials pledged to relocate businesses dealing in flammable chemicals from Old Dhaka. However, the relocation process has yet to resolve the longstanding problem.
The initial urgency following the disasters gradually faded, while chemical businesses continued operating in residential and commercial areas.
Reports from various non-governmental organisations indicate that Old Dhaka has around 25,000 chemical warehouses, of which 15,000 are located inside residential homes.
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has issued trade licences to only around 2,500 chemical businesses, according to the information provided.
Some traders have argued that establishing a dedicated chemical industrial zone outside Dhaka would benefit their businesses.
Visits to different parts of Old Dhaka reveal shops packed with plastic drums and containers of chemicals, as well as sacks containing combustible substances. Electrical wires often hang in tangled clusters above the shops, while residential homes occupy the floors above them.
Similar conditions can be found in Armanitola, Lalbagh, Kotwali, Bangshal and Chawkbazar.
The problem extends beyond individual shops. In many neighbourhoods, the ground floors of residential buildings house factories and warehouses storing chemicals and other flammable materials.
These include glycerin, anhydrous sodium compounds, sodium thiosulphate, hydrogen peroxide, methyl ethyl ketone, thinner and isopropyl alcohol. Improper storage and exposure to fire can make such substances hazardous.
The fire service has outlined several measures to reduce fire risks in Old Dhaka, including the following:
1. Relocating chemical warehouses
Move warehouses and factories storing chemicals, plastic raw materials and flammable substances out of residential buildings and densely populated areas to designated industrial zones, such as the BSCIC Chemical Industrial Estate.
Cancel licences for businesses storing chemicals commercially in residential buildings and take legal action against those operating in violation of regulations.
2. Improving building safety
Ensure compliance with the Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) in the construction of buildings and markets.
Provide adequate emergency exits and fire doors in high-rise buildings and markets, keeping them unlocked and free of obstructions.
Install and maintain fire detectors, fire extinguishers and functional hose systems in residential and commercial buildings.
3. Ensuring access to water
Install fire hydrants at street corners and near major markets to ensure adequate water supplies during emergencies.
Preserve ponds and other existing water bodies and maintain them for use by the Fire Service.
4. Improving roads and access routes
Widen narrow roads and alleys in phases to allow firefighting vehicles and equipment to reach fire sites.
Deploy small, rapid-response units and compact vehicles equipped with water-mist systems where larger fire engines cannot enter.
5. Maintaining gas and electricity lines
Regularly inspect and repair ageing electrical wiring, transformers and gas pipelines in coordination with the relevant utility providers, including Titas Gas, Desco and DPDC.
6. Raising public awareness
Conduct regular fire safety drills involving local business owners, employees and residents.
Train residents to use basic firefighting equipment and respond calmly during the first few minutes of a fire.
The Fire Service has said its efforts alone are insufficient to ensure safety in a traditional and densely populated area such as Old Dhaka. Coordinated initiatives by the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (Rajuk), the city corporation, Dhaka Wasa, business owners and landlords, alongside strict enforcement of the law, are essential.
Lt Col Md Mahmudul Hasan, director of operations and maintenance at the Fire Service and Civil Defence Department, said the presence of plastic and combustible materials had contributed to the severity of Monday’s fire.
“The primary cause of the severity of Monday’s fire was the presence of plastic and combustible materials. Although we have not yet been able to enter the premises, the way the smoke is billowing allows us to gauge the situation,” he said.
“Due to the narrow roads, Fire Service vehicles could not even enter the area, making rapid fire suppression impossible. Furthermore, there was no water source nearby. All in all, it took us about 12 hours to bring this fire under control.”
He said the fire service had made recommendations for Old Dhaka, including measures to facilitate firefighting and relocate chemical warehouses.
“However, these measures were never implemented. Cooperation from the city corporation, Rajuk and local residents is crucial to implementing these steps; otherwise, we will continue to witness tragedies like those of Churihatta and Nimtoli,” he added.
Fire Service sources said an investigation committee formed after the Churihatta fire on the night of February 20, 2019, recommended prohibiting chemical shops and warehouses in residential areas to prevent fire hazards.
Although some short-term measures were implemented, the long-term recommendations have not been fully realised. Chemical shops and warehouses have yet to be relocated in full, while most other recommendations also remain unimplemented.
As a result, Old Dhaka continues to face significant fire risks.
Abdullah Al Matin, a trader from Charakbazar, said the government had promised to provide traders with a designated location after the Nimtoli tragedy, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled.
“After the Nimtoli tragedy, the government promised to provide us with a designated location, but we have not received it to this day. We have yet to establish the proper environment required for this business. Consolidating the entire process within a single designated area would reduce the risk,” he said.
Efforts to remove illegal chemical shops from Old Dhaka began after the Nimtoli fire on June 3, 2010, which killed 124 people, including women and children.
In 2015, authorities planned to establish a chemical industrial zone, known as Chemical Village, on 20 acres of land in Sonabanda, Keraniganj. However, the project progressed slowly, and the land was later reallocated for an IT park.
Since the Churihatta tragedy, several other fires have occurred in Old Dhaka. The relocation of chemical facilities is often discussed after major incidents, but the issue gradually loses momentum.
In 2019, the DSCC launched a drive to evict hazardous chemical warehouses. The corporation later suspended the operation temporarily at the request of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI). The drive has not resumed since.
After the 2010 Nimtoli fire, a committee led by an additional secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs issued a 17-point directive to prevent similar accidents, including the removal of chemical warehouses from residential areas. Those recommendations remained unimplemented.
Another major tragedy followed on the night of February 20, 2019, when a fire broke out in Churihatta, Chawkbazar. An investigation committee formed by the Fire Service and Civil Defence subsequently issued several recommendations, identifying the large quantities of chemicals stored on the second, third and fourth floors of Wahed Mansion as the cause of the fire.

item.title: Cuet VC confined to office for 21 hours as students lock gate
item.description:
Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CuetT) Vice-Chancellor Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam has remained confined to his office for nearly 21 hours after protesting students locked the administrative building's main gate, demanding the reinstatement of former VC Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem.
The students locked the gate around 12:30pm on Monday, trapping the vice-chancellor and several others inside. Two people accompanying him fell ill and were taken to hospital around midnight.
As of 10am on Tuesday, students were still staging a sit-in in front of the administrative building.
Around 1:30am, reports emerged that two people inside the building had fallen ill. Dr Md Abdullah of the Cuet Medical Centre went to the scene to provide medical assistance.
The two, engineers Shahriar and Titu Mo Sohan, both Cuet alumni, received first aid before being taken to hospital for further treatment.
Asked about his health, Sheikh Shariful Alam said he was doing well.
“Two of our alumni members are suffering from complications related to high blood pressure, so I called for an ambulance and a doctor. Since everyone has been confined here for such a long time, they are feeling unwell and exhausted,” he said.
The vice-chancellor arrived at the Cuet campus in Raozan at 8:45am on Monday and entered the administrative building after breaking the lock on its front door. Students later locked the building’s main gate around 12:30pm. The water and electricity supplies were subsequently cut off.
Sheikh Shariful Alam, a professor at Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (Kuet), was appointed Cuet vice-chancellor on September 21.
Students had already been protesting the removal of former vice-chancellor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem and demanding his reinstatement. They have been enforcing a total shutdown since September 22.
University teachers, officers and staff have also been observing a work stoppage over the same demands. As a result, classes, examinations and other academic activities have remained suspended for nearly three weeks.

item.title: IMF: Bangladesh's GDP growth may drop to 3.2% in FY27
item.description:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected that Bangladesh's GDP growth may drop to 3.2% in the current fiscal year. This is 1.1 percentage points lower than its previous forecast.
Earlier, the ADB had projected a growth rate of 4% and the World Bank estimated it at 3.4%.
In a major blow to low-income people, prices of daily commodities are unlikely to fall anytime soon. During the same period, average inflation could rise to 10.9%.
This information was released on Tuesday (October 13) at the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group held in Bangkok.
The conference began on Monday (October 12) and will continue through October 18.
Against this backdrop, Finance Minister of Bangladesh Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury sought assistance from development partners, particularly the IMF and the World Bank, at the annual meeting in Bangkok.
The minister held meetings with IMF security director Urjit Patel and World Bank managing director Anna Bjerde.
The latest World Economic Outlook report shows that the global economy has maintained its resilience. However, sustaining this resilience is becoming increasingly costly.
According to forecasts, global growth is projected to be 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.
Soaring energy and food prices driven by the conflict in the Middle East are adversely impacting economic activity. However, investments in artificial intelligence (AI) are helping offset some of these losses.
Furthermore, global inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027.
Risks of economic deterioration remain, including a potential escalation of the conflict in the Middle East and a reassessment of AI-related expectations.
However, positive possibilities also exist: if AI investments prove durable, productivity surges rapidly, trade systems improve, and high fossil fuel prices accelerate investments toward energy security, economic conditions could improve.
The IMF noted that policy priorities include restoring the capacity of public finances, strengthening energy security, enhancing readiness for AI adoption, and keeping trade and cooperation channels open.

item.title: Gold prices cut by Tk3,266 per bhori
item.description:
Gold prices have fallen again in the domestic market, with the price of 22-carat gold reduced by Tk3,266 per bhori (11.664 grams).
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) announced the revised rates in a notification on Tuesday morning. The new prices came into effect at 10am.
Under the revised rates, 22-carat gold will sell for Tk228,031 per bhori.
The price of 21-carat gold has been reduced by Tk3,149 to Tk217,767 per bhori, while 18-carat gold will sell for Tk187,032 per bhori.
Gold produced using the traditional method will cost Tk152,798 per bhori.
Bajus said the prices include value-added tax (VAT), while making charges will be added separately depending on the design and craftsmanship of the jewellery.

item.title: Old Dhaka market fire under control after 12 hours, 4 firefighters sick
item.description:
A fire at Yusuf Khan Plaza Market in Chhota Katra of Chawkbazar in Old Dhaka was brought under control on Tuesday morning.
Fire Service personnel brought the blaze under control at 5:20am, although firefighting operations are still underway, said Md Talha Bin Jasim, an official of the media cell at the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters.
Meanwhile, four firefighters fell sick due to smoke from the fire and are under observation at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery.
The affected firefighters are Fire Fighter Md Zillur Rahman and Leader Md Nazrul Islam of Palashi Fire Station, Station Officer Md Maruf of Siddik Bazar Fire Station, and Leader Md Mahafuzur Haque Majumder of Khilgaon Fire Station.
According to Fire Service sources, the fire broke out at 5:02pm on Monday.
Initially, five units took part in the firefighting operation, but the number of units was later increased as the fire spread.

item.title: President stresses public awareness, preparedness to tackle disasters
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Tuesday stressed the need for preparedness, greater public awareness, disaster-resilient infrastructure and stronger early warning systems to mitigate the impact of natural disasters.
The government, relevant institutions and the public must work together to reduce disaster risks, said the president while addressing a programme marking the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction 2026 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka.
Bangladesh is a disaster-prone country where floods, cyclones, tidal surges, river erosion, landslides, droughts, lightning strikes and earthquakes pose persistent threats to people's lives and livelihoods, he said.
The adverse effects of climate change had further aggravated the situation, he said, adding that although Bangladesh contributed little to global warming, it had to bear a disproportionate share of its harmful consequences.
Referring to the devastating cyclone and tidal surge of 1970, the president said Bangladesh's history demonstrated the catastrophic consequences of natural disasters. “Such events not only claimed lives but also severely damaged livelihoods, the economy, infrastructure and overall development.”
He said disaster risks are increasing worldwide due to climate change, making the situation particularly concerning for vulnerable countries like Bangladesh.
Therefore, instead of focusing solely on disaster-related losses and damage, the country needed to strengthen preparedness and preventive measures well in advance, he added.
The president said Bangladesh has already made significant progress in disaster management.
Improved early warning systems, the establishment of shelters, volunteer networks and increased public awareness help reduce disaster-related deaths, but these initiatives need to be made more effective, he said.
He also drew the attention of the minister concerned to the need for law to ensure the protection of disaster management volunteers and recognise their contributions.
Expressing concern over the risks arising from unplanned urbanisation and weak infrastructure, the President said the potential consequences of an earthquake in Dhaka require particular attention.
Unplanned construction and inadequate urban planning could increase casualties during a major disaster, he said, stressing that the relevant authorities must ensure compliance with building safety regulations and implement proper urban planning.
He also highlighted the importance of maintaining the natural flow of rivers, preventing river pollution, improving drainage systems and protecting the environment to reduce disaster risks.
The ministries and institutions concerned must work in a coordinated manner to address these issues, he said.
Emphasising the role of local communities in disaster preparedness, the President said people in the haor areas of Sylhet demonstrated growing awareness by taking advance precautions and responding to early warnings.
Such initiatives needed to be expanded, he said, urging every family to keep essential documents and emergency supplies in safe places, respond promptly to early warnings and actively participate in disaster management activities.
The president said the government has undertaken various programmes to minimise disaster-related losses, adding that these initiatives must be implemented with sincerity and effective planning to reduce risks before disasters and ensure swift recovery afterwards.
To build a disaster-resilient Bangladesh, every home must be made safe, every family prepared and every community empowered, he said.
He also stressed the need to ensure transparency in development planning and policymaking, protect the environment and incorporate disaster risks into infrastructure development.
Calling for collective efforts to tackle disasters, the President said a resilient Bangladesh could be built through united initiatives, ensuring that people were protected from the impacts of disasters and could recover quickly in their aftermath.
Minister for Disaster Management and Relief Asadul Habib Dulu, State Minister for Disaster Management and Relief M Iqbal Hossain and Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief Munshi Rafiqul Alam were also present at the event.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 8th globally with ‘unhealthy’ air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 8th among the world's most polluted cities on Tuesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 158 at 9:52am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 201, while Singapore in Singapore and Delhi in India ranked second jointly with a score of 196, followed by Hanoi in Vietnam third place with an AQI score of 186.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: India detains top ‘cockroach’ leaders after flash protest
item.description:
India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said Tuesday that key leaders had been detained after entering an iconic protest site in New Delhi blocked by police.
Opposition parties and supporters of the movement have taken to the streets in recent days, defying a security clampdown to demand the resignation of the head of India’s election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.
Delhi Police said on Monday that Jantar Mantar in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites.
The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence.
But a video posted online by CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday showed protesters clambering over the barricades, running into the empty space and waving the national flag -- before police chased and detained them.
“CJP sneaks inside to reclaim Jantar Mantar,” the group said in a post on social media, adding that those detained included leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde.
“All of them have been detained by Delhi Police,” it added.
Delhi Police had announced three official sites on Monday as alternatives to Jantar Mantar, where protesters have gathered for decades -- including CJP demonstrations that led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal in July.
“You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke said, tagging Modi in his post.
Modi, in comments at a business conference in New Delhi on Tuesday, called India the “mother of democracy,” but did not refer directly to the protests.
“In our country, people openly debate a wide range of issues and discuss different perspectives,” he said.

item.title: Tahams opens fourth display center in Mirpur
item.description:
Tahams, one of Bangladesh’s emerging customized product brands, has officially opened its fourth Display Center in Mirpur Tuesday, expanding its personalized fashion, gifting, and lifestyle product experience for customers in the area.
The newly launched outlet allows customers to experience live customization and printing directly at the store.
From selecting designs to watching their chosen products being transformed through the customization process, customers can now enjoy a more interactive and engaging shopping experience.
Located at Al-Nahiyan Shopping Complex, Mirpur 1, the new Display Center features a wide range of customized products, including T-shirts available in sizes from 0 to 10XL, customized water bottles, mugs, and photo frames suitable for personal use, gifting, and special occasions.
Alongside Tahams’ core customization services, the outlet also showcases products from the brand’s other ventures, including Lumina by Tahams, Tahams Little Star, Perfume de Tahams, and Al Jamea, offering customers a diverse range of lifestyle products under one roof.
To celebrate the opening, Tahams has announced a Grand Opening Offer with up to 50% discount on selected products throughout the week.
“Customers will find aesthetic and customized T-shirts in every size, along with personalized water bottles, mugs, and photo frames. Our goal is to help people turn their creative ideas into products that reflect their personality and emotions,” said Israt Sultana Tohfa, founder of Tahams.
Founded in 2020 as an online T-shirt business, Tahams was started by Israt Sultana Tohfa, along with her husband Ashiq Ahmed, a computer engineer and photographer, and a few friends.
The brand has grown rapidly by focusing on customized fashion and personalized gifting solutions.
Today, Tahams’ product portfolio has expanded beyond customized T-shirts to include Panjabi, jeans, and apparel for customers of all ages and sizes, strengthening its position as a growing lifestyle brand in Bangladesh.
With the launch of its fourth Display Center, Tahams continues its mission of making customized fashion and lifestyle products more accessible while creating a space where customers can experience creativity, personalization, and quality under one roof.

Class I admissions by lottery, classes II–IX through written tests
item.description:
The Ministry of Education has issued an admission guidelines for government secondary schools for the 2027 academic year.

Under the new guideline, students seeking admission to Class I will be selected through a digital lottery, while admission to Classes II to IX will be based on written tests.

The ministry issued the guidelines on Tuesday. Applicants seeking admission to Class I may list up to five preferred schools. However, if an applicant selects both shifts at a school operating in two shifts, the two shifts will count as two separate choices.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) will centrally manage the digital lottery process for Class I admissions.

For Classes II to IX, students will be selected for vacant seats through written examinations, with admission determined by merit ranking. The admission test will carry 50 marks for Classes II to V and 100 marks for Classes VI to IX.

At a press conference in March, Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced that examinations would replace the lottery system for school admissions. Since then, educationists and other stakeholders have warned that introducing admission tests, particularly at the primary level, could put unnecessary pressure on children. They have also cautioned that it could increase dependence on coaching centres and private tuition, further widening inequalities in the education system. Allegations have already emerged that coaching activities have begun in different parts of Dhaka in preparation for the admission tests.

A subsequent decision was made to retain the lottery system for Class I admissions while introducing examinations for higher classes. Later, discussions were held on whether schools under the Ministry of Education could continue using the lottery system for Classes I to V, as before. However, that proposal was not adopted.

In the past, children had to face intense competition at a very young age in the name of school admission tests. Coaching centres and private tuition were common, and many families turned to coaching centres to secure places for their children in reputed schools. There were also allegations of irregularities, corruption and nepotism in the admission process. As a result, admission to good schools was difficult for many students from ordinary and low-income families. The issue had been widely debated in the media for years.

Against this backdrop, the lottery system was initially introduced only for Class I. From the 2011 academic year, government secondary schools offering Class I were required to admit students through a lottery instead of an admission test. The same system was introduced in private schools the following year. However, admissions to Classes II to IX continued to be conducted through examinations.

Later, amid the COVID-19 pandemic, the lottery system was introduced for all classes for the 2021 academic year. The practice continued thereafter. The latest guidelines now marks a change to that arrangement.

item.title: NYT, The Economist and AFP join AI copyright coalition
item.description:
Forty major media groups including The New York Times, The Economist and Agence France-Presse (AFP) have joined a global coalition of publishers that is seeking to prevent AI companies from using their journalism without permission, the group announced on Tuesday.

The coalition, known as SPUR (Standards for Publisher Usage Rights), was launched in February and already included media groups such as the BBC, The Financial Times and the Associated Press news agency as members.

The latest expansion doubles the number of publishers taking part, with the coalition aiming to help media companies track their content, highlight illegal copyright theft, and negotiate commercial deals with the AI groups behind services such as ChatGPT or Claude.

"There is rapidly growing momentum behind our effort to build a fairer, more sustainable information economy," David Buttle, co-founder and spokesperson for the SPUR Coalition, said in a statement.

"We know that high-quality journalism forms the foundations of AI models yet, as it stands, publishers have no mechanism to ensure they are fairly compensated for their work."

Fabrice Fries, the chairman and chief executive officer of Agence France-Presse (AFP), stressed that "each day, millions of people rely on AI assistants for information gathered and verified by news agency journalists."

"That original journalistic value must be recognised, credited and fairly compensated. Content traceability is not only a matter of intellectual property; it is also essential to maintaining public trust," he added in a statement.

Buttle called AFP''s decision to join the coalition "an important step in our growth".

"AFP is one of the world''s leading news agencies, and its journalism is of tremendous value to those developing AI systems. Too often, that value is captured without permission or compensation," he added.

Other news organisations which joined on Tuesday include US-based The Atlantic and Britain''s The Observer newspaper, Radio France, as well as publishers'' associations from Brazil, Japan, Argentina and Colombia.

Obtaining remuneration for their content is a vital issue for publishers whose traditional advertising-based business model has been undercut by social networks.

AI sites have also reduced the number of users going to internet news sites.

The New York Times sued OpenAI -- the maker of ChatGPT -- three years ago in a New York federal court for alleged theft of its copyrighted material used to train the company''s text-generating AI models.

The newspaper has accused OpenAI of committing "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" by using millions of news articles.

OpenAI has since signed content licensing deals with some news publishers around the world including The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, Le Monde in France and The Telegraph in Britain.

item.title: Ex-advisers condemn harassment of Prof Yunus at New York airport
item.description:
Former advisers to the interim government, led by Prof Muhammad Yunus, have strongly condemned “persistent harassment, online smear campaigns and targeted attacks” against the former chief adviser, including alleged harassment at New York airport.
“We express our unreserved outrage and strongest possible condemnation regarding the persistent harassment, online smear campaigns, and targeted attacks directed at former Chief Adviser, Nobel Laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus,” reads a joint statement issued by them on Tuesday.
The former advisers said the interim government did its best in addressing the Herculean task of rebuilding a nation at a time when Bangladesh stood on the precipice of total collapse following years of “unrestrained economic plunder, collapse of democratic institutions and corruption, systemic tyranny and gross violation of human rights”.
They claimed that the interim government put an end to heinous practices like enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings that were regularly committed under the fascist regime.
In February 2026, the interim government handed over power to a government elected through a free and fair general election, with the hope that the process of rebuilding the democratic institutions, ensuring justice for the victims of the fascist regime and defending human rights will continue in a sustained manner, the signatories said.
“​It is with deep regret that we notice that some political miscreants and a vested quarter are relentlessly spreading malicious misinformation and physically threatening Prof Yunus. We strongly condemn such cowardly tactics designed to create instability and undermine the credibility and wide acceptance of the interim government,” the statement reads.
The former advisers stated unequivocally that no amount of intimidation, falsehoods, online harassment, or personal threats will ever break their resolve for the changes July promised.
​The historic mandate of reform and dignity achieved by the people of Bangladesh and through enormous sacrifice of the youth cannot and will not be erased by malicious propaganda and attempts of an ousted fascist regime and its supporters, they said.
The signatories are former advisers Dr Salehuddin Ahmed, Dr M Fouzul Kabir Khan, CR Abrar, Dr Asif Nazrul, Adilur Rahman Khan, Lt Gen (retd) Jahangir Alam Choudhury, Brig Gen (retd) Dr Sakhawat Hussain, Faruk E Azam, Farida Akhter, Sharmeen Murshid, Mostofa Sarwar Farooki and Syeda Rizwana Hasan.
An attempt was made to harass Prof Yunus at the John F Kennedy Airport in New York, the United States, on Monday.

item.title: DC, SP rescue CUET VC after 30-hour confinement
item.description:
Vice-Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam was rescued by the Chittagong deputy commissioner and police superintendent on Tuesday evening after remaining confined to an administrative building for nearly 30 hours amid a student protest.
He was taken to Chittagong city for medical treatment.
Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police Mohammad Masud Alam rescued the vice-chancellor from Administrative Building-2 at around 6:00pm.
Earlier, at around 5:20pm, the two officials and other administration representatives arrived on the campus and held talks with the protesting students. They entered the building at around 5:50pm.
The deputy commissioner said they had come to ensure proper medical treatment for the vice-chancellor, who had fallen ill after being deprived of water and electricity for an extended period. He also assured the students that their demands would be conveyed to the government.
“He felt unwell after being without water and electricity for a prolonged period. Doctors have also advised him to receive advanced medical treatment. He contacted us by phone and through a live broadcast, seeking our assistance. We have come to take him for better treatment,” Zahidul Islam Mia said.
He added that the government was aware of the crisis on campus and expressed hope that it would be resolved soon.
The vice-chancellor and 11 others had remained confined to the building for nearly 30 hours without water, electricity or food supplies.
On September 21, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam of Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) was appointed CUET vice-chancellor, replacing Professor Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem.
Since September 22, students have been enforcing a “complete shutdown” programme demanding Sayem’s reinstatement. Teachers, officers and employees have also been observing work abstentions in support of the demand, bringing classes and examinations to a halt.
The new vice-chancellor had been unable to enter the campus following his appointment because of the protests. On Monday, however, he entered his office in the vice-chancellor’s building after breaking a lock placed by students, accompanied by leaders of the CUET unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal.
After learning of his arrival, students began gathering outside his office at around 9:30am and gave him a deadline to leave. When the deadline expired, they locked the building’s gate again at around noon and disconnected its water and electricity supplies.
The protesting students said they would remove the lock only if the vice-chancellor resigned, allowing him to leave the campus with dignity.

item.title: Prof Yunus’ harassment in US: New York Mission asked to take due legal action
item.description:
Strongly condemning the harassment of former interim government Chief Adviser Professor Dr Muhammad Yunus at John F Kennedy Airport in New York, US, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has asked its Mission in New York to take up the matter with local law enforcing agencies.
The MoFA, in a statement, also said it asked the Bangladesh Mission in New York to identify the perpetrators and take due legal action against those who have tarnished the image of Bangladesh and all its citizens before the world.
“The government of Bangladesh strongly condemns the harassment of former interim government chief adviser Professor Dr Muhammad Yunus at John F Kennedy Airport in New York, US,” said the ministry.
It appears that a group of perpetrators suspected to be linked with the Bangladesh Awami League, were behind this harassment committed against Nobel Peace Prize laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus on foreign soil, the government said, noting that Prof Yunus is highly respected by the international community.
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said the government will take necessary measures over the harassment of Prof Yunus.
Any attempt by Awami League leaders or activists living abroad to engage in such acts would not go unchallenged, he said at a press briefing on the progress of various government activities at Secretariat.
Dr Yunus is currently in the US, where an attempt was made to harass him at an airport, he said, adding that the incident is believed to be linked to Dr Yunus taking responsibility for running the state after Sheikh Hasina fled the country.

item.title: Four injured in gas cylinder blast at Savar CNG station
item.description:

According to police and local sources, the cylinder exploded while an empty truck was being refuelled, injuring four people at the scene.
The injured were taken to Enam Medical College Hospital in Savar. One of them reportedly suffered serious eye injuries.
